title: Best Healthcare & Medical Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Proton Mail, Signal and ExpressVPN compared on end-to-end encryption, HIPAA Business Associate Agreements, telehealth security and data-broker protection.
intro: Your medical data is incredibly valuable to data brokers and advertisers. From health apps selling your information to unsecured telehealth platforms, protecting your healthcare privacy requires the right tools and knowledge of HIPAA gaps.

products.name: Signal
products.tagline: End-to-end encrypted messaging for healthcare communications
pros: Open source; its encryption protocol has been independently analysed
cons: Requires both parties to use Signal
Doesn't sign HIPAA Business Associate Agreements

products.name: Proton Mail
products.tagline: Encrypted email for secure healthcare correspondence
products.pricing: Free plan; Mail Plus from about $4/month billed yearly
pros: Messages can be set to expire
Signs a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement on request
cons: End-to-end encryption to non-Proton addresses needs a password-protected message or PGP

products.name: ExpressVPN
products.tagline: Paid VPN that encrypts your connection to its servers
products.pricing: Subscription (Basic, Advanced and Pro plans); cheaper per month on longer terms
pros: Kill switch (Network Lock) blocks traffic if the VPN drops
cons: Encrypts your connection, not the messages themselves

features.name: End-to-End Encryption
features.description: Ensures your medical communications can only be read by you and your intended recipient

protonmail.note: Automatic between Proton Mail users; password-protected messages to others

expressvpn.note: Encrypts traffic between your device and the VPN server; that isn't end-to-end encryption of your messages

features.name: HIPAA-Friendly Features
features.description: Tools and settings that help maintain HIPAA compliance for healthcare communications

signal.note: Doesn't sign Business Associate Agreements, so providers can't use it for patient data under HIPAA

protonmail.note: Proton signs a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) on request

expressvpn.note: Not a communications service; Business Associate Agreements not assessed

features.name: Telehealth Security
features.description: Protection for video calls and online medical consultations

expressvpn.note: Encrypts your connection on public Wi-Fi and hides it from your ISP; the telehealth platform secures the call

features.name: Data Broker Protection
features.description: Prevents health data from being collected and sold to third parties

signal.note: Keeps almost no user data; no ads

protonmail.note: Zero-access encrypted mailbox; funded by subscriptions, not ads

expressvpn.note: Hides browsing from your ISP; its tracker blocker is on the Advanced and Pro plans only

features.name: Ease of Use
features.description: How simple it is to set up and use for healthcare privacy protection

protonmail.note: Familiar email interface; encrypting to non-Proton addresses takes extra steps

verdict.summary: Proton Mail scores highest on these five criteria: its email is end-to-end and zero-access encrypted, and Proton will sign a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement. Signal comes next, with end-to-end encrypted messages and calls, but it doesn't sign Business Associate Agreements, so healthcare providers generally can't use it for patient information. ExpressVPN scores lowest: it encrypts your connection on public Wi-Fi and hides it from your internet provider, but a VPN is not end-to-end encryption.

bestFor.reason: Encrypted email, and Proton signs a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement on request

bestFor.useCase: Private health conversations with family or friends
bestFor.reason: End-to-end encrypted messages and calls, with disappearing messages
Encrypts your connection on untrusted networks and hides it from your ISP

pro_tips: Use a private browser window, or a browser that blocks ads, when you research health conditions online, so ad networks have less to build a medical profile from.
Use your provider's patient portal for messages about your care, since providers must use services that sign HIPAA agreements; use Signal for health conversations with family or friends.
Use a VPN like ExpressVPN when accessing telehealth platforms from public WiFi or unsecured networks to protect your medical consultations.
Create a separate Proton Mail address specifically for healthcare communications to compartmentalize your medical privacy.
Regularly audit your health apps' privacy settings and delete those that share data with third parties - many period trackers and fitness apps share data with advertisers.

faqs.question: Are health apps covered by HIPAA?
faqs.answer: Most health apps are NOT covered by HIPAA. Only apps used directly by HIPAA-covered entities (like hospitals) are protected. Consumer health apps, fitness trackers, and period trackers can legally sell your data to advertisers and data brokers.

faqs.question: Can I use these tools for telehealth appointments?
faqs.answer: Usually you'll join through the platform your provider chooses, because providers must use services that sign a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement, which Signal does not. You can still join from an up-to-date browser or the provider's app, and a VPN such as ExpressVPN adds encryption when you're on public Wi-Fi.

faqs.question: How do I protect my period tracking data?
faqs.answer: Avoid apps that share data with third parties. Choose an app that keeps data on your device or encrypts it, or track offline, and turn off the app's location access if it doesn't need it. A VPN hides your IP-based location, but not what you enter into the app.

faqs.question: What medical information do data brokers collect?
faqs.answer: Data brokers collect prescription purchases, health app data, fitness tracker information, search history for medical conditions, and location data from medical facilities. They create detailed health profiles sold to insurers, employers, and marketers.

faqs.question: Is encrypted email necessary for healthcare communications?
faqs.answer: While not legally required for patient communications, encrypted email protects sensitive health information from being intercepted, stored by email providers, or accessed by hackers. It's especially important for reproductive health information and mental health communications.
